key_results: Breakup clouds are oblate and lateral to flow. Evaporation alone predicts survival orders longer; breakup sharply increases surface area and vaporization.
No-breakup >500 mm for ≥40 μm; KH-RT predicts ≤2.97 mm through 120 μm; WERT49 predicts 0.075–11.96 mm for 1–120 μm.

mechanisms.summary: Model-based interpretation: tiny KH children evaporate nearly immediately; larger RT-scale children persist and spread while evaporating.

evidence_candidates.claim: Evaporation alone cannot explain the observed ~10.9 mm droplet-survival region; concurrent breakup is required in the model interpretation.
Existing shock-driven breakup models predict faster extinction than some observed droplets under the detonation's variable acceleration.
